n.0: It is a base, but a pH below 7 describes an acid; bases have a pH above 7.
n.1: An acid would turn the blue strip red and leave the red strip unchanged, which is the opposite of what was seen.
n.3: A neutral solution would not change the color of either litmus strip.

S.q: A ruler is marked in millimeters (every 0.1 cm). The tip of a leaf lies about halfway between the 6.3 cm and 6.4 cm marks. Which recording follows the standard rule for reporting a measurement?
o: 6.4 cm
6.3 cm
S.w: A measurement is reported to one estimated digit beyond the smallest marking. The smallest marking is 0.1 cm, so the student reports to 0.01 cm: 6.35 cm.

n.1: Two digits beyond the smallest marking claims more precision than a millimeter ruler can give.
n.2: Rounding up to the next mark throws away the estimated digit and misstates the length.
n.3: This stops at the smallest marking and drops the estimated digit the scale allows.

S.q: When phospholipids are placed in water, they arrange themselves into a double layer. Which feature of phospholipid structure explains this arrangement?
o: Their tails are polar and are attracted to the surrounding water.
Their hydrophilic heads face water while hydrophobic tails face inward.
Their three fatty acid tails make them dissolve in water.
Their nonpolar heads face water while polar tails face inward.
S.w: A phospholipid has a hydrophilic (polar) phosphate head and two hydrophobic (nonpolar) fatty acid tails. In water the heads face outward and the tails hide inside, forming a bilayer.

n.0: The fatty acid tails are nonpolar and hydrophobic, so they avoid water.
n.2: Phospholipids have two fatty acid tails (triglycerides have three), and the tails repel water.
n.3: Polarity is reversed: the heads are polar and the tails are nonpolar.

S.q: Place these events of a typical 28-day ovarian and uterine cycle in order, starting with day 1 of the cycle.
o: Estrogen from growing follicles rebuilds the endometrium (proliferative phase)
The functional layer of the endometrium is shed (menstrual phase)
An LH surge causes the dominant follicle to release a secondary oocyte
The corpus luteum degenerates and progesterone levels fall
Progesterone from the corpus luteum makes the endometrium secretory
S.w: Days 1 to 5: menstrual phase, as the functional layer is shed. Days 6 to 14: FSH-stimulated follicles secrete estrogen that rebuilds the endometrium (proliferative phase). About day 14: high estrogen triggers the LH surge and ovulation. Days 15 to 28: the corpus luteum secretes progesterone and the endometrium is secretory. Without pregnancy, the corpus luteum degenerates near the end of the cycle, progesterone falls, and menstruation begins again.

S.q: Researchers randomly select 200 adults from a city patient registry, then let each person decide whether to use a new sleep app. After a month they compare hours of sleep between users and nonusers. What is the main weakness of this design?
o: There is no comparison group for the app users.
The 200 participants were not randomly sampled.
Hours of sleep should be the independent variable.
The participants were not randomly assigned to groups.
S.w: Random assignment reduces bias. When participants choose their own group, the groups may differ in other ways (people who choose a sleep app may already care more about sleep), which confounds the result. Random sampling, which this study did use, only makes the sample representative of the registry.

n.0: The nonusers form a comparison group; the problem is that people chose which group to join.
n.1: The 200 adults were drawn at random from the registry, so the sample is random; the problem is how they were sorted into groups.
n.2: Hours of sleep is what the researchers measure, so it is the dependent variable; app use is the independent variable.

S.q: A lab report lists a healthy adult's red blood cell count as 5.2 × 10⁶ cells per microliter of blood. How is this count written in standard form?
o: 520,000 cells
S.w: A positive exponent of 6 moves the decimal point 6 places to the right: 5.2 becomes 5,200,000.

n.0: This moves the decimal point 5 places (5.2 × 10⁵).
n.1: This moves the decimal point 7 places (5.2 × 10⁷).
n.2: This treats the exponent as negative and moves the decimal point to the left.

S.q: Which pair of values is typical for a healthy adult breathing quietly at rest?
o: Tidal volume about 150 mL; 12 to 20 breaths per minute
Tidal volume about 1,200 mL; 12 to 20 breaths per minute
Tidal volume about 500 mL; 60 to 100 breaths per minute
Tidal volume about 500 mL; 12 to 20 breaths per minute
S.w: A normal resting breath moves about 500 mL (tidal volume), and a resting adult breathes about 12 to 20 times per minute.

n.0: About 150 mL is the anatomical dead space of the conducting zone, not the whole tidal volume.
n.1: About 1,200 mL is a typical residual volume, far larger than one quiet breath.
n.2: 60 to 100 per minute is the normal resting heart rate, not the breathing rate.

S.q: A nurse pours 30 mL of cough syrup from a tall, narrow bottle into a wide, shallow dosing cup. The syrup takes the shape of the cup but still measures 30 mL. Which description of the syrup's particles explains this behavior?
o: They are squeezed by the cup walls into the new shape
They are far apart and move freely to fill any container
They stay close together but can slide past one another
They vibrate in fixed positions that hold a set volume
S.w: Liquids have a definite volume but no definite shape. Their particles stay close together (so the volume stays 30 mL) but can slide past one another (so the syrup flows into the shape of the cup).

n.0: Liquids are nearly incompressible; the volume stays 30 mL, so the particles are not being pushed closer together.
n.1: Particles that are far apart and move freely describe a gas, which would spread to fill the whole container instead of keeping 30 mL.
n.3: Particles vibrating in fixed positions describe a solid, which keeps its own shape instead of taking the shape of the cup.

S.q: A science teacher lists four well-established statements on the board. Which statement is best classified as a scientific theory rather than a scientific law?
o: At constant temperature, a gas's pressure varies inversely with its volume.
In a closed system, total mass is the same before and after a reaction.
Two masses attract with a force that depends on their masses and distance.
All living things are made of cells, and new cells come from existing cells.
S.w: Cell theory is a broad explanation of how living things are organized and reproduce, supported by many observations. The other statements describe consistent, often mathematical, patterns without explaining why, which is what laws do.

n.0: This is Boyle's law, a mathematical description of a pattern in gases.
n.1: This is the law of conservation of mass: a description of what always happens in reactions.
n.2: This is the law of gravitation, a mathematical description of the attraction between masses.

S.q: In a healthy adult, how is most of the oxygen in arterial blood carried to the tissues?
o: Bound to hemoglobin inside red blood cells
Bound to albumin and other plasma proteins
As bicarbonate ions carried in the plasma
Dissolved directly in the plasma around the cells
S.w: About 98.5% of oxygen travels bound to hemoglobin in red blood cells as oxyhemoglobin; only about 1.5% is dissolved in plasma.

n.1: Albumin maintains osmotic pressure and carries some drugs and hormones; it is not an oxygen carrier.
n.2: Bicarbonate is the main carrier form of carbon dioxide, not oxygen.
n.3: Oxygen dissolves poorly in plasma, so only about 1.5% is carried this way.

S.q: A cardiologist describes damage to the layer of the heart wall that contracts to pump blood. Which choice names that layer and its tissue correctly?
o: Myocardium, a layer of cardiac muscle
Endocardium, a layer of cardiac muscle
Myocardium, a layer of smooth muscle
Epicardium, a layer of cardiac muscle
S.w: The myocardium is the thick middle layer of the heart wall, made of cardiac muscle, and it contracts to pump blood; it is the layer damaged in a heart attack. The epicardium and endocardium are thin non-muscular coverings.

n.1: The endocardium is a thin lining of endothelium and connective tissue over the chambers and valves; it does not contract.
n.2: The layer is right, but the myocardium is cardiac muscle (striated, branched, with intercalated discs); smooth muscle lines vessels and hollow organs.
n.3: The epicardium (visceral pericardium) is a thin serous membrane on the heart surface; it contains no contractile muscle.

S.q: A nutrition student is classifying carbohydrates found in foods and in the body. Which of these are polysaccharides? Select all that apply.
o: Glycogen
Starch
Lactose
Cellulose
Sucrose
Glucose
S.w: Starch (plant storage), glycogen (animal storage) and cellulose (plant cell walls) are polysaccharides, long chains of glucose units.

n.2: Lactose is a disaccharide (glucose + galactose).
n.5: Glucose is a monosaccharide, the monomer of these polysaccharides.

S.q: A lab report lists three elements measured in a patient's blood tests by their symbols: K, Na and Fe. Which names match these symbols, in the same order?
o: Krypton, sodium, iron
Potassium, nitrogen, iron
Potassium, sodium, iron
Calcium, sodium, iron
S.w: Several symbols come from Latin names: K is potassium (kalium), Na is sodium (natrium) and Fe is iron (ferrum).

n.0: Krypton's symbol is Kr. K is potassium.
n.1: Nitrogen's symbol is N. Na is sodium.
n.3: Calcium's symbol is Ca. K is potassium.

S.q: In a sealed flask, 10.0 g of baking soda reacts completely with 20.0 g of vinegar, producing carbon dioxide gas that stays inside the flask. What is the total mass of the flask's contents after the reaction?
o: Less than 30.0 g, because a gas has very little mass
Less than 30.0 g, because some mass is converted into energy
More than 30.0 g, because a new compound has formed
Exactly 30.0 g, because atoms are rearranged, not lost
S.w: The law of conservation of mass: atoms are rearranged in a reaction, not created or destroyed, so the total mass of the products equals the total mass of the reactants (10.0 g + 20.0 g = 30.0 g) in a closed system.

n.0: Gas does have mass; in a sealed flask the carbon dioxide is still counted. Mass would seem to drop only if the gas escaped from an open container.
n.1: In ordinary chemical reactions the mass change from energy release is far too small to measure; mass is conserved.
n.2: Forming a new compound rearranges the same atoms, so the total mass does not increase.

S.q: A nursing student documents a healing wound on day 3. Which of her notes records quantitative data?
o: The wound measures 2.4 cm in length.
The patient describes the pain as sharp.
The dressing has a faint sour odor.
The wound edges look pink and dry.
S.w: Quantitative data are numbers with units, such as a length of 2.4 cm. Descriptions of color, odor or pain quality are qualitative.

n.1: A word describing pain quality is qualitative; a 0 to 10 pain score would be quantitative.
n.2: An odor description is qualitative.
n.3: Color and texture are descriptions, which makes them qualitative data.

S.q: Place pure water and three aqueous solutions, each made with 1 mole of solute per kilogram of water, in order of freezing point, starting with the highest freezing point.
o: Calcium chloride (CaCl₂) solution
Sodium chloride (NaCl) solution
Glucose solution
Pure water
S.w: Freezing point depression is a colligative property: the more dissolved particles, the lower the freezing point. Pure water has no solute particles (freezes at 0 °C). Glucose dissolves as 1 particle per unit, NaCl gives 2 ions, and CaCl₂ gives 3 ions, so the CaCl₂ solution has the lowest freezing point.

S.q: A pea plant has purple flowers and the genotype Pp, where P (purple) is dominant over p (white). Which statement about this plant is correct?
o: It is heterozygous, and purple is its phenotype.
It is homozygous, and Pp is its phenotype.
It is heterozygous, and purple is its genotype.
It carries two different genes for flower color.
S.w: Pp has two different alleles, so the plant is heterozygous. Its genotype is Pp; its observable trait (phenotype) is purple flowers.

n.1: Homozygous means two identical alleles (PP or pp), and Pp is a genotype, not a phenotype.
n.2: Genotype and phenotype are swapped: Pp is the genotype and purple is the phenotype.
n.3: Pp is two different alleles of one gene, not two different genes.

S.q: A student compares two tomato plants. Plant A gets fertilizer and sits in a sunny window; Plant B gets no fertilizer and sits in a shaded hallway. Plant A grows taller. What is the main flaw in this design?
o: Two variables differ, so the cause is unclear.
Plant height should be plotted on the x-axis.
The dependent variable should be fertilizer.
There is no control group to compare against.
S.w: A fair test changes one variable at a time. Fertilizer and light both differ, so the extra growth cannot be credited to fertilizer; light could explain it.

n.1: Height is the dependent variable, which belongs on the y-axis.
n.2: Fertilizer is what the student changes, so it is the independent variable, not the dependent variable.
n.3: Plant B, with no fertilizer, is meant as the comparison; the problem is that it also differs in light.

S.q: A runner moves from sea level to train at high altitude for two months. Place the events in the order they occur as her body adjusts, starting with the first.
o: The kidneys detect a low blood oxygen level
The blood's oxygen-carrying capacity rises over weeks
The kidneys release erythropoietin (EPO)
Red bone marrow increases red blood cell production
Less oxygen reaches the blood from the thinner air
S.w: High altitude means less oxygen enters the blood. The kidneys sense the low oxygen and release EPO, a hormone that signals red bone marrow to make more red blood cells. Over weeks, the extra red blood cells raise the blood's capacity to carry oxygen.

S.q: A tutor asks a student to identify correct statements about periodic trends for the main-group elements. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.
o: Electronegativity is highest at the lower left of the table
Ionization energy increases down a group
Metallic character increases down a group
Atomic radius increases left to right across a period
Electronegativity increases left to right across a period
Atomic radius increases down a group
S.w: Down a group, atoms gain shells, so radius and metallic character increase. Across a period, nuclear charge rises, so electronegativity increases (and radius decreases).

n.0: Electronegativity is highest at the upper right (fluorine); the lower left holds the least electronegative elements.
n.1: Ionization energy decreases down a group because outer electrons are farther from the nucleus and easier to remove.
n.3: Atomic radius decreases across a period as more protons pull the same shells inward.

S.q: A survey of 2,000 nursing students finds that those who drink more energy drinks also report higher anxiety levels. Which conclusion is justified by this survey?
o: Cutting out energy drinks will lower students' anxiety.
Energy drinks cause anxiety in nursing students.
Anxiety causes students to drink more energy drinks.
Energy-drink use and anxiety are linked in this group.
S.w: A survey is observational: it shows an association (correlation) but cannot show which variable causes which, or whether a third factor, such as exam stress, drives both.

n.0: This predicts the effect of an intervention, which requires evidence of causation.
n.1: Concluding causation from a correlation is the classic error; only a controlled experiment can show it.
n.2: Reversing the direction is still a causal claim the survey cannot support.

S.q: A study guide asks where the autonomic nervous system fits in the overall organization of the nervous system. Which statement places it correctly?
o: It is the sensory division of the central nervous system
It is a branch of the somatic division that serves the internal organs
It is a branch of the central nervous system that controls skeletal muscle
It is a motor (efferent) branch of the peripheral nervous system
S.w: The PNS has a sensory (afferent) division and a motor (efferent) division. The motor division splits into the somatic division (skeletal muscle) and the autonomic division (cardiac muscle, smooth muscle and glands), which in turn splits into sympathetic and parasympathetic divisions.

n.0: The autonomic nervous system is a motor division of the PNS, not a sensory part of the CNS.
n.1: Somatic and autonomic are sister branches of the motor division; the autonomic division is not part of the somatic division.
n.2: Skeletal muscle is controlled by the somatic division, and the autonomic division belongs to the PNS, not the CNS.

S.q: A high school wrestler develops a red, ring-shaped, scaly rash and is diagnosed with tinea corporis (ringworm). Which type of medication is appropriate for this infection?
o: An antiviral
An antibiotic for bacteria
An antihelminthic for worms
An antifungal
S.w: Despite its name, ringworm (tinea) is a fungal skin infection, so it is treated with an antifungal.

n.0: Antivirals target viruses; tinea is caused by a fungus.
n.1: Antibiotics target bacteria; tinea is caused by a fungus.
n.2: Ringworm is not caused by a worm; the name comes from the ring-shaped rash.

S.q: A student is summarizing the structure of the epidermis for a study guide. Which statements about the epidermis are accurate? Select all that apply.
o: Its melanocytes lie mainly in the stratum corneum
It is stratified squamous epithelium
It is avascular
Most of its cells are keratinocytes
It is built mainly of collagen and elastin
Its deepest layer is the stratum corneum
S.w: The epidermis is keratinized stratified squamous epithelium with no blood vessels of its own (it is nourished from the dermis). Keratinocytes are its most numerous cells.

n.0: Melanocytes lie in the stratum basale, the deepest layer.
n.4: Collagen and elastin fibers are features of the dermis, which is connective tissue.
n.5: The stratum corneum is the most superficial layer; the deepest is the stratum basale.

S.q: A home pregnancy test detects a hormone in urine shortly after a blastocyst implants. Which statement correctly identifies this hormone and its role in early pregnancy?
o: hCG from the mother's anterior pituitary, which keeps the corpus luteum alive
Progesterone from the corpus luteum, which keeps the endometrium intact
hCG from the embryo's trophoblast, which keeps the corpus luteum alive
LH from the mother's anterior pituitary, which triggers implantation
S.w: Pregnancy tests detect hCG, secreted by the trophoblast of the implanted blastocyst (later the placenta). hCG keeps the corpus luteum alive so it keeps secreting progesterone, which maintains the endometrium.

n.0: hCG is made by the embryo's trophoblast, not by the mother's pituitary.
n.1: Progesterone does maintain the endometrium, but home pregnancy tests detect hCG, not progesterone.
n.3: LH triggers ovulation, not implantation, and it is not the hormone pregnancy tests detect.

S.q: In the classification of bones by shape, to which category does the patella (kneecap) belong?
o: Irregular
Flat
Sesamoid
Short
S.w: Sesamoid bones form within tendons, and the patella is the classic example. Short bones are cube-like (carpals, tarsals), flat bones are thin (cranial bones, sternum, ribs, scapulae) and irregular bones include the vertebrae.

n.0: Irregular bones, such as the vertebrae, have complex shapes and do not develop within tendons.
n.1: Flat bones are thin and often curved, such as the cranial bones, sternum, ribs and scapulae.
n.3: Short bones are roughly cube-shaped, such as the carpals and tarsals, and do not form inside tendons.

S.q: A student is reviewing the features of spongy (cancellous) bone. Which statements about spongy bone are accurate? Select all that apply.
o: Its spaces hold red marrow in flat bones
It forms the dense outer wall of the diaphysis
It fills the epiphyses of long bones
Its basic units are tightly packed osteons
It is built from a lattice of trabeculae
S.w: Spongy bone is a lighter network of trabeculae whose spaces hold red marrow. It fills the epiphyses of long bones and the interior of flat bones and vertebrae. Compact bone, built of osteons, forms the dense outer layer, including the wall of the diaphysis.

n.1: The dense outer wall of the diaphysis is compact (cortical) bone; spongy bone is light and porous.
n.3: Osteons (Haversian systems) are the units of compact bone; spongy bone is organized as trabeculae without osteons.

S.q: A pharmacy technician sorts four samples on a shelf. Which of these samples is a homogeneous mixture?
o: Oil and vinegar dressing
Distilled water
Sand stirred into water
Salt dissolved in water
S.w: Salt water is a solution, a homogeneous mixture: the dissolved salt is spread evenly, so every part has the same composition, and the proportions can vary.

n.0: Oil and vinegar separate into visible layers, so the dressing is a heterogeneous mixture.
n.1: Distilled water is a pure substance, the compound H₂O, not a mixture.
n.2: Sand does not dissolve and settles out, so sand in water is a heterogeneous mixture (a suspension).

S.q: The mRNA codons GGU, GGC, GGA and GGG all code for the amino acid glycine. Which property of the genetic code does this illustrate?
o: Universality: nearly all organisms share the same code
Redundancy: several codons can specify one amino acid
Punctuation: stop codons mark where a protein ends
Ambiguity: one codon can specify several amino acids
S.w: The genetic code is redundant (degenerate): 61 codons code for 20 amino acids, so most amino acids have more than one codon.

n.0: The code is nearly universal, but the example is about multiple codons for glycine, not about different organisms.
n.2: Stop codons (UAA, UAG, UGA) code for no amino acid; the example involves codons for glycine.
n.3: The code is unambiguous: each codon specifies one meaning. The example shows several codons for one amino acid, the reverse.

S.q: When acidic chyme enters the duodenum, a hormone is released that signals the pancreas to secrete a fluid rich in bicarbonate. Which hormone sends this signal?
o: Secretin
Glucagon
Cholecystokinin
Gastrin
S.w: Secretin from the duodenum causes the pancreas to release bicarbonate, which neutralizes acid chyme arriving from the stomach.

n.1: Glucagon is an islet hormone that raises blood glucose and does not control bicarbonate.
n.2: Cholecystokinin mainly triggers pancreatic enzyme release and gallbladder contraction.
n.3: Gastrin is a stomach hormone that increases acid secretion, the opposite of neutralizing it.

S.q: An adult has burns covering the entire right arm and the entire front of the trunk. Using the adult rule of nines, what percentage of total body surface area is burned? Enter a whole number.

tr.18: counting the front of the trunk as 9%, like an arm (9 + 9)
tr.36: counting the arm as 18%, the value for a leg (18 + 18)
tr.45: adding the back of the trunk as well (9 + 18 + 18)

S.w: Adult rule of nines: each arm is 9% and the front of the trunk is 18%. 9 + 18 = 27%.

S.q: A student views a blood smear through a compound light microscope with a 10x eyepiece (ocular lens) and a 40x objective lens. Enter the total magnification as a whole number.

tr.4: Divided the objective by the eyepiece.
tr.40: Used the objective lens alone and left out the eyepiece.
tr.50: Added the two lenses (10 + 40) instead of multiplying them.

S.w: Total magnification = ocular magnification x objective magnification = 10 x 40 = 400 (400x).

S.q: Place the links in the chain of infection in order, starting with the infectious agent and ending with the person who becomes infected.
o: Mode of transmission
Susceptible host
Infectious agent
Reservoir
Portal of exit
Portal of entry
S.w: The pathogen (infectious agent) lives in a reservoir, leaves through a portal of exit, travels by a mode of transmission, enters a new host through a portal of entry, and infects a susceptible host. Breaking any link stops the spread.

S.q: Place the levels of structural organization in order from the simplest to the most complex, starting with the simplest.
o: Cellular
Chemical
Organism
Organ system
Organ
Tissue
S.w: Atoms and molecules (chemical level) build cells (cellular level). Similar cells form tissues, two or more tissue types form an organ, organs that cooperate form an organ system, and all the organ systems together make up the organism.

S.q: Which of the following are part of the second line of defense, the internal nonspecific (innate) defenses? Select all that apply.
o: Plasma cells secreting antibodies
Complement proteins
Fever
Cytotoxic T cells
Natural killer cells
Lysozyme in saliva
S.w: Second-line defenses act inside the body and are nonspecific: phagocytes, NK cells, inflammation, fever, complement proteins and interferons.

n.0: Antibody-secreting plasma cells belong to the third line, adaptive humoral immunity.
n.3: Cytotoxic T cells are antigen-specific lymphocytes of the third line, adaptive cell-mediated immunity.
n.5: Lysozyme in saliva and tears is a first-line, external barrier defense.

S.q: The ventral body cavity is subdivided by a dome-shaped muscle that contracts during breathing. Which two cavities does the diaphragm separate?
o: The pleural and pericardial cavities
The abdominal and pelvic cavities
The cranial and vertebral (spinal) cavities
The thoracic and abdominopelvic cavities
S.w: The diaphragm separates the thoracic cavity (lungs, heart) above from the abdominopelvic cavity below.

n.0: The pleural and pericardial cavities both lie within the thoracic cavity above the diaphragm.
n.1: The abdominal and pelvic cavities are continuous, both within the abdominopelvic cavity below the diaphragm.
n.2: The cranial and vertebral cavities form the dorsal cavity; the diaphragm is part of the ventral cavity.

S.q: The same arm muscles are used to lift a pencil and then a heavy suitcase. How does the nervous system chiefly increase the force the muscle produces for the suitcase?
o: Each fiber contracts harder in response to a single impulse
More motor units are recruited to contract at once
The myosin filaments lengthen to form more cross-bridges
More troponin is released from the sarcoplasmic reticulum
S.w: A single fiber follows the all-or-none principle, so whole-muscle force is graded by recruiting more motor units (one motor neuron plus all the fibers it supplies) and by raising the frequency of stimulation.

n.0: Each fiber responds all-or-none to an impulse; force is graded at the level of the whole muscle.
n.2: Myofilaments keep their length during contraction; they slide past one another.
n.3: The sarcoplasmic reticulum releases Ca²⁺, not troponin; troponin is part of the thin filament.

S.q: The DNA double helix has the same width along its entire length. Which feature of base pairing explains this uniform width?
o: Each base pair joins a purine with a pyrimidine.
Adenine pairs with guanine, both double-ring bases.
Each base pair joins two single-ring pyrimidines.
Each base pair joins two double-ring purines.
S.w: Every pair joins a double-ring purine (A or G) with a single-ring pyrimidine (T or C), so each rung of the ladder is the same width.

n.1: Adenine pairs with thymine, not guanine; A-G pairing is a common error.
n.2: Two pyrimidines would make a pair narrower; each pair contains one purine.
n.3: Two purines would make a pair wider than the others; A pairs with T and G pairs with C.

S.q: A student is reviewing a cross section of the spinal cord. Which statements about the spinal cord are accurate? Select all that apply.
o: Its dorsal root ganglia hold the cell bodies of sensory neurons
Its dorsal roots carry motor commands out to skeletal muscles
In adults it ends at about the L1 to L2 vertebral level
Its outer layer is gray matter, as in the cerebral cortex
Its gray matter lies inside, surrounded by white matter
It gives rise to 12 pairs of spinal nerves
S.w: In the spinal cord, butterfly-shaped gray matter lies inside white matter. Dorsal root ganglia contain sensory neuron cell bodies, and in adults the cord ends at about L1 to L2, below which the cauda equina continues.

n.1: Dorsal roots are sensory; motor commands leave through the ventral roots.
n.3: The spinal cord is the reverse of the cerebrum: its gray matter is inside and its white matter outside.
n.5: There are 31 pairs of spinal nerves; 12 pairs is the number of cranial nerves.

S.q: Two parents are both carriers (Aa) of an autosomal recessive disorder. Their first three children are unaffected. What is the chance that their fourth child will be affected?
o: Very high, since three children are already unaffected
3 in 4, since that is the share expected to show the trait
1 in 16, using the product rule across two children
1 in 4, the same as for each of the earlier children
S.w: Each fertilization is independent. For Aa x Aa, every child has a 1/4 chance of being aa, whatever happened with earlier children.

n.0: A 3:1 ratio is a probability for each child, not a quota the family must fill.
n.1: 3/4 is the chance a child is unaffected (AA or Aa), not affected.
n.2: The product rule gives the chance of two specified events together; the question asks about one child.

S.q: A chemistry worksheet shows the expression 3 Ca(OH)₂, meaning three formula units of calcium hydroxide. How many atoms in total does this expression represent? Enter your answer as a whole number.

tr.5: Counted one formula unit and ignored the coefficient 3.
tr.9: Did not apply the subscript 2 to both O and H inside the parentheses (3 x 3).
tr.12: Applied the subscript to hydrogen but not to oxygen (3 x 4).

S.w: One Ca(OH)₂ contains 1 Ca, 2 O and 2 H (the subscript 2 applies to everything inside the parentheses), which is 5 atoms. The coefficient 3 multiplies the whole unit: 3 x 5 = 15 atoms (3 Ca, 6 O, 6 H).

S.q: Activity of a human enzyme at five temperatures: 20 °C, 15 units; 30 °C, 30 units; 37 °C, 42 units; 45 °C, 20 units; 55 °C, 3 units. What is the best prediction for activity at 65 °C?
o: Lower than at 55 °C, since activity falls past the optimum
About 42 units, since the enzyme has hit its maximum
Higher than at 55 °C, since the activity cycles up and down
Higher than at 37 °C, since heat speeds up reactions
S.w: Enzyme activity rises to an optimum (37 °C here) and then falls as heat denatures the enzyme. Activity is already only 3 units at 55 °C, so at 65 °C it should be even lower, close to zero.

n.1: The maximum of 42 units occurred at 37 °C; activity has fallen steeply since then.
n.2: The data show a rise-then-fall pattern, not a repeating cycle.
n.3: Heat speeds reactions only up to the optimum; above it the enzyme denatures and activity drops, as the data show.

S.q: Each kidney contains about a million microscopic units, each able to filter blood and form urine on its own. What is this functional unit of the kidney called?
o: Renal corpuscle
Nephron
Renal pyramid
Glomerulus
S.w: The nephron is the functional unit of the kidney: it filters blood, reabsorbs and secretes substances, and forms urine. Each kidney has approximately one million.

n.0: The renal corpuscle (glomerulus plus capsule) is the filtering part of a nephron, not the whole unit.
n.2: A renal pyramid is a region of the medulla containing parts of many nephrons and collecting ducts.
n.3: The glomerulus is the capillary tuft where filtration happens; it is only one part of a nephron.

S.q: A meal contains bread, lean turkey and butter. When the resulting chyme first enters the duodenum, which statement about the chemical digestion of this meal is accurate?
o: Protein digestion has begun; starch and fat digestion have not
Starch and protein digestion have begun; most fat digestion has not
Starch digestion has begun; protein and fat digestion have not
Fat and protein digestion have begun; starch digestion has not
S.w: Step 1: starch digestion begins in the mouth with salivary amylase. Step 2: protein digestion begins in the stomach with pepsin. Fat digestion is mostly in the small intestine, after bile and pancreatic lipase act (lingual lipase does very little), so most fat digestion has not yet occurred.

n.0: Starch digestion began in the mouth with salivary amylase, before the stomach.
n.2: Protein digestion has already begun in the stomach by the time chyme reaches the duodenum.
n.3: Most fat digestion waits for bile and pancreatic lipase in the small intestine, while starch digestion began in the mouth.

S.q: When the right ventricle contracts, blood leaves it through which valve and enters which vessel?
o: The pulmonary valve, into the pulmonary trunk
The aortic valve, into the aorta
The pulmonary valve, into the pulmonary veins
The tricuspid valve, into the pulmonary trunk
S.w: The right ventricle pumps deoxygenated blood through the pulmonary (semilunar) valve into the pulmonary trunk, which divides into the pulmonary arteries to the lungs.

n.1: The aortic valve and aorta are the exit route from the left ventricle.
n.2: Pulmonary veins return blood from the lungs to the left atrium; they do not connect to the right ventricle.
n.3: The tricuspid valve lies between the right atrium and right ventricle, at the entrance to the ventricle, not its exit.

S.q: A cell has a membrane-bound nucleus, mitochondria and a cell wall, but no chloroplasts. Of the following, which is the most likely source of this cell?
o: A yeast cell
A Staphylococcus bacterium
A moss leaf cell
A human liver cell
S.w: Step 1: a nucleus and mitochondria mean the cell is eukaryotic, which rules out bacteria. Step 2: a cell wall without chloroplasts fits a fungus such as yeast, which has a chitin wall and cannot photosynthesize.

n.1: Bacteria have cell walls but are prokaryotes, so they have no nucleus or mitochondria.
n.2: A moss leaf cell has a wall and nucleus, but as a photosynthetic leaf cell it contains chloroplasts.
n.3: Human cells are eukaryotic with mitochondria, but animal cells have no cell wall.

S.q: A muscle cell completely breaks down one molecule of glucose by aerobic cellular respiration. Which of these are products of the process? Select all that apply.
o: Molecular oxygen
Carbon dioxide
ATP
Lactic acid
Glucose
Water
S.w: Aerobic respiration: C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6 O₂ -> 6 CO₂ + 6 H₂O + energy (ATP and heat).

n.0: Oxygen is a reactant of aerobic respiration; it is released by photosynthesis.
n.3: Lactic acid is made by fermentation when oxygen is lacking, not by complete aerobic breakdown.
n.4: Glucose is the fuel (reactant) being broken down, not a product.

S.q: Place these levels of skeletal muscle organization in order from largest to smallest, starting with the whole muscle.
o: Myofilament (actin or myosin)
Whole muscle wrapped in epimysium
Myofibril
Sarcomere
Fascicle wrapped in perimysium
Muscle fiber wrapped in endomysium
S.w: A muscle (epimysium) contains fascicles (perimysium), each a bundle of muscle fibers, which are single cells (endomysium). Each fiber is packed with myofibrils, which are chains of sarcomeres, the contractile units built from thin actin and thick myosin myofilaments.

S.q: A glowing wooden splint smolders slowly in air, but when it is placed in a jar of pure oxygen, it bursts into flame. Which factor best explains the faster reaction in pure oxygen?
o: A higher concentration of one of the reactants
A larger surface area of the wood exposed in the jar
A lower activation energy for oxygen in a closed jar
A catalyst present in pure oxygen but missing in air
S.w: Air is only about 21% oxygen. In pure oxygen, there are many more O₂ molecules per unit volume, so they collide with the wood far more often. Raising the concentration of a reactant increases the reaction rate.

n.1: The splint is the same piece of wood in both cases, so its surface area has not changed.
n.2: Activation energy is a property of the reaction pathway; it changes when a catalyst is added, not when oxygen is concentrated.
n.3: Oxygen is a reactant in combustion, not a catalyst, and the rate rises because there is more of it.

E.q: The patient's admission record lists chronic kidney disease among her conditions. Based on its root, what does the word chronic indicate about the disease?
o: It persists over a long time
It has been present since birth
It spreads from person to person
It started suddenly and is severe
E.w: The root chron means time, so a chronic condition is one that lasts a long time (the opposite of acute).

n.1: Present from birth is congenital (con- = with, gen = birth), not chronic.
n.2: Spreading between people describes a contagious disease; nothing in chron refers to spread.
n.3: A sudden, severe onset describes an acute condition; chron refers to time, meaning long-lasting.

E.q: A nurse is ending an email to her unit manager that requests a change to next month's schedule. Which closing sentence is most appropriate?
o: Let me know ASAP, since I already told my family I'd be off that weekend.
Thanks in advance for approving this change to my schedule.
Thank you for considering my request; I am glad to discuss it at any time.
I trust you will approve this request, as I have certainly earned it by now.
E.w: A professional email closes courteously, thanks the reader and offers to follow up.

n.0: "ASAP" and the assumption that the request is already approved are too informal and presumptuous.
n.1: Thanking the manager in advance "for approving" assumes the answer and pressures the reader.
n.3: The demanding tone pressures the manager and is not respectful.

E.q: A clinic manager wants to say that no more than two nurses are scheduled on weekends. Which sentence places the limiting word so that it states this meaning most clearly?
o: The clinic only schedules two nurses on weekends.
Only the clinic schedules two nurses on weekends.
The clinic schedules only two nurses on weekends.
The clinic schedules two nurses only on weekends.
E.w: A limiting word such as only, just, nearly or almost goes directly before the word it limits. To limit the number, "only" goes before "two nurses."

n.0: Placed before the verb, "only" limits "schedules" (it schedules and does nothing else), not the number two.
n.1: Placed before "the clinic," "only" means no other place schedules two nurses, which is a different meaning.
n.3: Placed before "on weekends," "only" means nurses are scheduled on weekends and not on weekdays.

E.q: In Carmen's formal outline, a main point is labeled I. and its first supporting idea is labeled A. How should she label a specific detail that supports idea A?
o: II.
B.
a.
E.w: A formal outline moves from broad to specific as I., A., 1., a. A detail supporting a capital-letter point therefore takes an Arabic numeral: 1.

n.0: II. marks the next main point at the highest level of the outline.
n.1: B. would mark a second supporting idea at the same level as A., not a detail beneath A.
n.3: Lowercase a. is the next level down, used for a detail under a numbered point such as 1.

E.q: A volunteer is writing a short guide for first-time blood donors. Place the sentences in the order that creates the most logical paragraph, starting with the first sentence.
o: After the donation, rest for about 15 minutes and have a snack.
First, drink plenty of water the day before your appointment.
Next, eat a meal rich in iron a few hours before you arrive.
Following these steps can help you feel well during and after your visit.
Before you donate blood, a few simple steps can help you prepare.
E.w: The topic sentence introduces the steps. "First" and "Next" give the steps before donating, "After the donation" follows them in time, and the concluding sentence sums up the benefit of the steps.

E.q: Andre is writing a cover letter to the human resources department of a regional hospital. Which sentence is most appropriate for this letter?
o: I am eager to bring my CNA experience to your medical-surgical unit.
I'm really excited about this job, and I know I'd be a great fit.
I am, without question, the most qualified applicant you will receive.
I need a full-time job with good benefits, and your hospital offers both.
E.w: A cover letter calls for a formal, confident and respectful tone that links the applicant's experience to the employer's needs.

n.1: The contractions and the vague "great fit" are too casual and give the employer no specific reason to hire.
n.2: The boastful claim sounds arrogant and cannot be supported, which suits no professional application.
n.3: The sentence focuses on what the writer wants rather than what the writer offers the hospital.

E.q: A nurse is writing a reference letter for a former nursing aide: "Ms. Alvarez was ___ about following every infection-control step." Which word completes the sentence with the most positive connotation?
o: persnickety
obsessive
meticulous
nitpicky
E.w: All four words describe close attention to detail, but only "meticulous" has a positive, professional connotation.

n.0: "Persnickety" is informal and suggests fussing over trivial details, a negative connotation.
n.1: "Obsessive" suggests an unhealthy fixation, a negative connotation in a reference letter.
n.3: "Nitpicky" is informal and suggests petty fault-finding, a negative connotation.

E.q: A unit secretary is writing a note about a lost staff badge. Which sentence uses apostrophes correctly?
o: The nurses dont know whose badge was left in the lounge.
The nurses don't know whose badge was left in the lounge.
The nurse's don't know whose badge was left in the lounge.
The nurses don't know who's badge was left in the lounge.
E.w: "Nurses" is a plain plural (no apostrophe), "don't" is a contraction of "do not" (apostrophe where the o is missing), and "whose" is a possessive pronoun (no apostrophe).

n.0: The contraction of "do not" needs an apostrophe: "don't".
n.2: "Nurses" is a plain plural subject, so it takes no apostrophe.
n.3: "Who's" means "who is"; the possessive needed here is "whose".

E.q: Ms. Ortiz is grading research papers for a nursing prerequisite course. Which situation in a student's paper is an example of plagiarism?
o: Quoting a sentence word for word with quotation marks and a citation
Using another writer's idea in her own words without naming the source
Summarizing an article's main points in her own words with a citation
Stating that the skeleton supports the body without giving a citation
E.w: Plagiarism is presenting another person's words or ideas as your own. Rewording an idea does not make it yours, so a borrowed idea without credit to its source is plagiarism.

n.0: Exact words in quotation marks with a citation give full credit, which is correct use of a source.
n.2: A summary in the writer's own words with a citation credits the source properly.
n.3: That the skeleton supports the body is common knowledge, which needs no citation.

E.q: An editor is checking adverbs formed by adding -ly in a discharge leaflet for patients. Which adverb is spelled correctly?
o: finaly
gentlely
carefuly
publicly
E.w: "Publicly" is formed by adding -ly straight to public; it is the standard exception to the -ically pattern.

n.0: Final + ly keeps both l's: "finally".
n.1: Adjectives ending in -le replace the e with y: gentle becomes "gently".
n.2: Careful + ly keeps both l's: "carefully".

E.q: A clinic is writing a handout for patients who have no medical training. Which sentence is best suited to these readers?
o: Pt should obtain BP readings BID and document all of the findings.
Check your blood pressure at the same time each morning and evening.
Check your systolic and diastolic pressure each morning and evening.
Patients with hypertension should monitor their BP readings diurnally.
E.w: Plain language for a lay audience uses everyday words, short sentences and clear actions, without jargon or slang.

n.0: Clinical abbreviations (Pt, BP, BID) are jargon meant for health professionals, not patients.
n.2: The action is clear, but "systolic" and "diastolic" are medical terms a lay reader may not know.
n.3: "Hypertension," "BP" and "diurnally" are technical terms a lay reader may not understand.

E.q: The cardiologist examined the pericardium for signs of infection after the patient's chest surgery. Based on its prefix, where is the pericardium located?
o: Around the heart
Beside the heart
Within the heart
Below the heart
E.w: peri- means around and cardi/o means heart, so the pericardium is the sac that surrounds the heart.

n.1: Beside is a meaning of para-, the look-alike prefix; peri- means around.
n.2: Within would use endo- or intra- (the endocardium lines the inside of the heart).
n.3: Below would use sub- or hypo-, not peri-.

E.q: Read the paragraph from an infection-control newsletter. (1) Hand washing is one of the most effective ways to prevent infections in hospitals. (2) Washing for at least 20 seconds removes most germs from the skin. (3) Alcohol-based sanitizers work well when hands are not visibly dirty. (4) Many nurses say they prefer unscented soaps to scented ones. (5) Staff who clean their hands between patients protect everyone on the unit. Which sentence should be removed to improve the paragraph's unity?
o: Sentence 2
Sentence 3
Sentence 5
Sentence 4
E.w: Every sentence should support the topic sentence: hand hygiene prevents infections. Sentence 4 mentions soap, but a preference for unscented soap says nothing about preventing infection, so it breaks unity.

n.0: Sentence 2 explains how long to wash, which directly supports the topic of preventing infection.
n.1: Sentence 3 adds a second hand-hygiene method, so it supports the topic.
n.2: Sentence 5 explains who benefits from hand hygiene, so it supports the topic.

E.q: A student is checking whether sentences about a retired nurse contain a dependent clause. Which sentence is complex?
o: The nurse trained me, and she retired last spring.
The nurse who trained me retired last spring.
The nurse trained me and retired last spring.
Trained by experts, the nurse retired last spring.
E.w: Two steps: "who trained me" has its own subject (who) and verb (trained), so it is a dependent relative clause; with the independent clause "The nurse retired last spring", the sentence is complex.

n.0: Two independent clauses with no dependent clause make a compound sentence.
n.2: One subject with two verbs is a simple sentence with a compound predicate.
n.3: "Trained by experts" is a participial phrase (no subject-verb pair), so the sentence is simple.

E.q: A certified nursing assistant is charting a routine check. Which sentence keeps verb tense consistent?
o: The aide checked the patient's temperature and recorded it in the chart.
The aide checked the patient's temperature and records it in the chart.
The aide checks the patient's temperature and recorded it in the chart.
The aide checks the patient's temperature and had recorded it in the chart.
E.w: Both actions happened in the same past visit, so both verbs stay in the simple past: "checked ... recorded."

n.1: The sentence shifts from past ("checked") to present ("records") for two actions in the same visit.
n.2: The sentence shifts from present ("checks") to past ("recorded") with no reason for the change.
n.3: The past perfect "had recorded" places the recording before the checking, which is illogical, and it shifts tense.

E.q: A writer wants to set off an interrupting phrase that already contains commas and to give it more emphasis than parentheses would. Which punctuation should enclose the phrase?
o: A pair of colons
A pair of dashes
A pair of semicolons
A pair of brackets
E.w: A pair of dashes works like a pair of commas or parentheses but gives more emphasis, and it can enclose an element that has its own internal commas.

n.0: A colon introduces a list, explanation or quotation after an independent clause; colons are not used in pairs.
n.2: Semicolons join independent clauses or separate complex series items; they do not enclose interrupters.
n.3: Brackets mark the writer's own insertions inside a quotation.

E.q: After the patient's femur fracture, the orthopedic team placed his leg in traction until surgery could be scheduled. Based on its root, what does traction apply to the leg?
o: A twisting force that turns the limb
A steady pulling force on the limb
A brace that carries the limb's weight
A cut that opens the limb's tissue
E.w: The root tract means pull, so traction is a steady pulling force (used to align a broken bone).

n.0: Turning is the meaning of vert/vers, not tract.
n.2: Carrying is the meaning of port, not tract.
n.3: Cutting is the meaning of sect (as in dissect), not tract.

E.q: Before discharge, the nurse reviewed the postoperative care instructions with the patient's family. Based on the prefix, when are these instructions meant to be followed?
o: Before the surgery
Between two surgeries
During the surgery
After the surgery
E.w: post- means after, so postoperative care is the care given after an operation.

n.0: Before surgery is preoperative; pre- means before.
n.1: Between is the meaning of inter-, not post-.
n.2: During surgery is intraoperative; intra- means within.

E.q: A student is studying verbal phrases for an English quiz. Which sentence contains an infinitive phrase?
o: The patient went to the cafeteria after lunch.
The patient wanted to rest after lunch.
The patient resting after lunch felt better.
Resting after lunch helped the patient.
E.w: An infinitive is "to" + the base form of a verb: "to rest" (to rest after lunch) is an infinitive phrase.

n.0: "To the cafeteria" is "to" + a noun, which is a prepositional phrase, not an infinitive.
n.2: "Resting after lunch" is a participial phrase describing "patient".
n.3: "Resting after lunch" is a gerund phrase acting as the subject.

E.q: Noah is writing a report on flu vaccine safety for his health class. Which source would be the most credible for his report?
o: A CDC web page on vaccine safety updated this year
A federal fact sheet on flu vaccines published in 2009
A health magazine article quoting two family doctors
A vaccine maker's web page summarizing its own trials
E.w: A credible source is current, written by experts, and free of a conflict of interest. The CDC page meets all three tests; the 2009 fact sheet is outdated, the maker's page is biased, and the magazine article is a secondhand report for general readers.

n.1: It comes from an expert agency, but a 2009 fact sheet is out of date for a report on flu vaccines, which are reformulated every season.
n.2: A popular magazine article is a secondhand account written for general readers; the agency that monitors vaccine safety is a more authoritative source.
n.3: The manufacturer profits from the vaccine, so its summary of its own trials has a conflict of interest.

E.q: In a retrospective study, researchers reviewed ten years of patient records to see whether earlier screening had changed outcomes. Based on its word parts and the context, what does retrospective mean?
o: Looking back at past events
Looking across several groups
Looking ahead to future events
Looking within one person
E.w: retro- means backward and spect means look, so retrospective means looking back. The context (reviewing ten years of past records) confirms it.

n.1: Across is trans-, not retro-.
n.2: Looking ahead is the meaning of pro- or pre- words such as prospective; retro- means backward.
n.3: Within is intra- or endo-, not retro-.

E.q: A state board newsletter is being edited for concise wording. Which sentence is the most concise version that keeps the full meaning?
o: To renew a license, it is required that nurses in this state complete 24 hours of continuing education.
To renew, nurses must complete 24 hours.
In order to renew a license, nurses in this state must complete 24 hours of continuing education.
To renew a license, nurses in this state must complete 24 hours of continuing education.
E.w: Concise does not mean shortest. The best version removes padding ("in order to," "it is required that") and keeps every detail.

n.0: "It is required that" is a wordy construction; "must" says the same thing more directly.
n.1: This version drops what is renewed, the state, and the type of hours, so it loses meaning.
n.2: "In order to" adds words without adding meaning; "to" alone is enough.

E.q: A lab supervisor is writing a note that begins with an introductory dependent clause. Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
o: Because the hematology lab closed early on Friday afternoon the samples were stored until Monday.
Because the hematology lab closed early on Friday afternoon, the samples, were stored until Monday.
Because the hematology lab closed early on Friday afternoon, the samples were stored until Monday.
Because, the hematology lab closed early on Friday afternoon, the samples were stored until Monday.
E.w: A long introductory dependent clause (Because the hematology lab closed early on Friday afternoon) is followed by a comma before the main clause.

n.0: The comma after the long introductory dependent clause is missing, so the reader runs "afternoon the samples" together.
n.1: A comma must not separate the subject (the samples) from its verb (were stored).
n.3: No comma follows the subordinating conjunction "Because".

E.q: An editor is checking a clinic newsletter for sentence errors. Which of the following is a comma splice?
o: The bus was late; we missed the appointment.
The bus was late, so we missed the appointment.
The bus was late, we missed the appointment.
Because the bus was late, we missed the appointment.
E.w: A comma splice joins two independent clauses with only a comma. "The bus was late" and "we missed the appointment" can each stand alone.

n.0: A semicolon correctly joins two independent clauses.
n.1: A comma plus the coordinating conjunction "so" correctly joins two independent clauses.
n.3: The first clause is dependent (Because ...), so a comma after it is correct.

E.q: A hospital volunteer is writing an announcement about a parade route. Which of the following words, all ending in a "seed" sound, is spelled correctly?
o: superceed
preceed
proceed
excede
E.w: Only three common words end in -ceed: exceed, proceed and succeed. Only supersede ends in -sede. All others end in -cede.

n.0: Supersede is the one common word ending in -sede; "superceed" wrongly gives it the -ceed ending.
n.1: Precede takes the regular -cede ending; -ceed is reserved for exceed, proceed and succeed.
n.3: Exceed is one of the three -ceed words, so "excede" is wrong.

E.q: The committee was persuaded by the epidemiologist's credible account of how the outbreak began in a school cafeteria. Based on its root, what does credible mean?
o: Able to be dictated
Able to be believed
Able to be visualized
Able to be recognized
E.w: The root cred means believe, and -ible means able to be, so credible means believable.

n.0: Saying is the meaning of dict, as in dictate.
n.2: Seeing is the meaning of vis/vid, as in visualize and visible.
n.3: Recognizing (knowing) is the meaning of cogn, as in recognize and cognitive.

E.q: Kenji reduces a six-page article on diabetes prevention to three sentences, in his own words, that state the article's main ideas, and he cites the article. What has Kenji written?
o: A direct quotation
A summary
A paraphrase
A reference entry
E.w: A summary gives only the main ideas of a source, in the writer's own words, and is much shorter than the original. Like a paraphrase, it must be cited.

n.0: A direct quotation reproduces the source's exact words in quotation marks; Kenji used his own words.
n.2: A paraphrase restates one specific passage at about the same length; Kenji condensed a whole article to three sentences.
n.3: A reference entry lists a source's publication details at the end of the paper; it does not restate ideas.

E.q: Ana's peer reviewer leaves two comments: (1) "Your second paragraph doesn't connect to your thesis," and (2) "You wrote 'effect' where you mean 'affect.'" Which statement correctly classifies the work these comments call for?
o: Both comments call for revising, since both change the draft.
Comment 1 calls for revising, and comment 2 calls for editing.
Comment 1 calls for editing, and comment 2 calls for revising.
Both comments call for proofreading, since both point out errors.
E.w: Step 1: a paragraph that does not support the thesis is a content and organization problem, so fixing it is revising. Step 2: choosing affect instead of effect is a word-usage correction at the sentence level, so fixing it is editing.

n.0: Any fix changes the draft, but a usage error like affect/effect is corrected in editing, not revising.
n.2: This swaps the two stages: connecting a paragraph to the thesis is revising, and fixing a word error is editing.
n.3: Proofreading is the last check for typos; reworking a paragraph so it supports the thesis is revising.

E.q: Read the sentence: "The reason the test was delayed is because the machine broke." Which revision corrects the faulty sentence structure?
o: The reason the test was delayed, is that the machine broke.
The reason the test was delayed is because of the machine broke.
The reason the test was delayed is that the machine broke.
The reason the test was delayed is when the machine broke.
E.w: "The reason ... is" must be completed by a noun clause (that the machine broke), not an adverb clause beginning with "because". This repairs the faulty predication.

n.0: A comma must not separate the subject (The reason the test was delayed) from its verb (is).
n.1: "Because of" must be followed by a noun phrase, not a clause with a verb (broke).
n.3: "Is when" is also faulty predication: a reason is not a time.

E.q: Read the sentence from a hospital policy summary: "The new policy is meant to reduce wait times, improving patient satisfaction, and to lower costs." Which revision corrects the faulty parallelism?
o: Change "to lower" to "lowering."
Change "to reduce" to "reducing."
Change "improving" to "to improve."
Delete the word "and" before "to lower."
E.w: Two of the three items are infinitives (to reduce, to lower). Changing "improving" to "to improve" makes all three match.

n.0: This leaves "to reduce" as an infinitive while the other two items are gerunds, so the list is still mixed.
n.1: This leaves "to lower" as an infinitive while the other two items are gerunds, so the list is still mixed.
n.3: Removing "and" does not change the forms of the items and also leaves the series without its conjunction.

E.q: A nurse's comment is split by a dialogue tag in a staff story. Which version is punctuated and capitalized correctly?
o: "I can't stay," Leah said. "because my shift starts at noon."
"I can't stay", Leah said, "because my shift starts at noon."
"I can't stay," Leah said, "because my shift starts at noon."
"I can't stay," Leah said, "Because my shift starts at noon."
E.w: Two steps: the quotation is one sentence interrupted by the tag, so a comma follows the tag and the second part continues in lowercase. In US style the comma after "stay" goes inside the quotation mark.

n.0: A period after "said" would start a new sentence, which would need a capital; but "because ..." continues the first sentence, so a comma is needed.
n.1: In US style the comma goes inside the closing quotation mark.
n.3: The second part continues the same sentence, so "because" is not capitalized.

E.q: A pharmacy student is comparing products in a study guide. Which sentence uses a comparative or superlative form correctly?
o: The night shift is more busier than the day shift on most weekends.
Of the three dressings, the foam one is the least painful to remove.
Of the two inhalers, the blue one is the most effective for her asthma.
Of the three textbooks, this one is the better choice for anatomy.
E.w: With three or more items, use the superlative (-est, most, least). Three dressings are compared, so "least painful" is correct.

n.0: "More busier" is a double comparative; use "busier" alone.
n.2: Comparing exactly two items calls for the comparative: "the more effective."
n.3: Comparing three or more items calls for the superlative: "the best choice."

E.q: A nurse educator is titling a patient handout and must use standard title case. Which title is capitalized correctly?
o: A guide to caring for patients in the home
A Guide to Caring for Patients in the Home
A Guide To Caring For Patients In The Home
a Guide to Caring for Patients in the Home
E.w: In title case, capitalize the first and last words and all major words (nouns, verbs, adjectives); lowercase articles and short prepositions in the middle (to, for, in, the).

n.0: This is sentence case; title case capitalizes the major words such as Guide, Caring, Patients and Home.
n.2: Short prepositions (to, for, in) and articles (the) in the middle of a title are lowercase in title case.
n.3: The first word of a title is always capitalized, even when it is an article.

E.q: A staff memo describes a charge nurse in several ways. Which sentence contains an appositive phrase?
o: Ms. Lee, the charge nurse, approved the schedule.
Ms. Lee, approving the schedule, thanked the charge nurse.
Ms. Lee approved the schedule for the charge nurse.
Ms. Lee, who is the charge nurse, approved the schedule.
E.w: An appositive phrase is a noun phrase that renames the noun beside it: "the charge nurse" renames Ms. Lee.

n.1: "Approving the schedule" is a participial phrase.
n.2: "For the charge nurse" is a prepositional phrase.
n.3: "Who is the charge nurse" has a subject and a verb, so it is a relative (dependent) clause, not a phrase.

E.q: A hospital historian is writing about staff hired decades ago. Which sentence uses plurals and apostrophes correctly?
o: Several RNs' on the unit were hired in the 1990s.
Several RNs on the unit were hired in the 1990s'.
Several RNs on the unit were hired in the 1990s.
Several RN's on the unit were hired in the 1990s.
E.w: Plurals of abbreviations and numbers add s with no apostrophe: RNs, 1990s. Nothing in the sentence is possessive.

n.0: "RNs'" is a plural possessive, but the RNs do not own anything here.
n.1: A decade written in numerals takes s with no apostrophe: "1990s".
n.3: An apostrophe is not used to form the plural of an abbreviation such as RN.

E.q: A pharmacy newsletter is printing a short problem-and-solution paragraph. Place the sentences in the order that creates the most logical paragraph, starting with the first sentence.
o: Many patients forget to take their evening medications.
Another option is a phone alarm set for the same time each night.
Together, these tools can help patients stay on schedule.
One simple solution is a weekly pill organizer with a labeled slot for each day.
E.w: The paragraph states the problem first, then gives solutions: "One simple solution" introduces the first, "Another option" adds the second, and "Together" sums up both tools. "These tools" must follow the sentences that name them.

E.q: A staff newsletter describes a nurse's family. Which sentence uses the correct plural of the compound noun?
o: Both of her sisters-in-law work as nurses.
Both of her sister-in-laws work as nurses.
Both of her sister's-in-law work as nurses.
Both of her sisters-in-laws work as nurses.
E.w: In a hyphenated compound noun, the main word takes the plural: sister becomes sisters, giving "sisters-in-law".

n.1: The s goes on the main word (sister), not the end of the compound.
n.2: An apostrophe shows possession, not plurality; nothing is owned here.
n.3: The compound is pluralized once, on the main word; adding a second s is wrong.
